entities.span: Run every ground truth pair against the current scoring configuration and report which fell outside their expected band. Run it whenever the scoring prompt or the model changes
rejected_spans: so a swap is checked rather than hoped about

entities.span: **Done when:** one command runs the whole set and prints a per pair pass or fail with the actual score,
a regression on any pair is visible in the output,
and the run works against a changed model with no code edit.
Design it (spec): `/architect eval harness runner` · written 2026-09-08, 11 acceptance criteria.
rejected_spans: Settles the three decisions spec 0016's Follow up handed over (rerun count, the stability probe pass rule, what `tags`/`acceptableBands` mean to pass or fail), plus two load bearing constraints found during design rather than named up front: the harness has to live under `test/` (not beside feature 15's data in `src/`) since the real scoring path needs the fixture session minting that root `AGENTS.md` forbids an application module from importing, and a usage gate refusal is a third outcome of a real scoring call that needed its own handling. A cross check on a different model found real gaps in the first draft, most load bearing a majority vote with no tie break rule and a preference leak check that could never fire on the real committed data; both were rewritten and verified against the repo before this was accepted

entities.span: Build it: `/develop eval harness runner` · code in `test/eval/`, `test/helpers/eval-verdict.ts`, `test/setup/eval-filter.ts`, `src/features/scoring/eval/band-anchors-hash.ts`

Project scaffolding: the `eval` Vitest project (`extends: true`, its own timeouts and `maxConcurrency`, `fileParallelism: false`), the `pnpm eval` script, and the shared `resolvedModel()`/`bandAnchorsHash()` helpers, satisfies AC-1, AC-2, AC-9, AC-11

Verdict logic: the pure rerun outcome classification, majority vote with its no majority and `acceptableBands` exception, the `stability-probe` rule, and the `preference-isolation` baseline comparison, each proved against constructed fixtures with no vendor call, satisfies AC-3, AC-4, AC-5, AC-6.
rejected_spans: 25 tests in `test/helpers/eval-verdict.test.ts`; each rule broken on purpose after the commit hooks ran, seven of eight mutations caught, the eighth exposed a redundant presence check that is now compiler enforced instead

entities.span: The harness itself: the thin thread against one real pair, then the full sixteen with bounded concurrency and the run's own aggregate exit code, satisfies AC-1, AC-2, AC-7, AC-8, AC-9.
rejected_spans: The full set ran for real on 2026-09-08: 80 vendor calls, 132 seconds, 14 of 16 pairs passed, exit code 1

entities.span: The drift guard: the committed `BAND_ANCHORS` snapshot test under the free unit suite, and the gitignored output directory, satisfies AC-10.
rejected_spans: Proved by rewording an anchor (both assertions fail) and by changing only the hash function's separator (the text assertion still passes, the hash one fails), so the second is demonstrably not a duplicate of the first

entities.span: Verify it: `/check verify eval harness runner` · PASS 2026-09-08, all 11 acceptance criteria met, 13 of 13 `verify.md` steps run and passed.
rejected_spans: AC-11 was proved harder than the checklist asks: `ai_scoring` was repointed at a different vendor and model entirely (Google `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`), and the harness scored 5 of 5 and reported the new model with zero edits under `test/eval/`. The run level abort was proved free by engaging the real kill switch: exit code 1, all sixteen pairs `INCOMPLETE`, and zero occurrences of `inconclusive` anywhere in the output, which is the distinction AC-3 exists to protect. Exactly one fixture user was observed alive at peak across a full sixteen pair run, proving one session serves the whole run, and none was left behind. The harness's own first finding is recorded below and belongs to the scorer, not to this feature
entities.unclassified_note: A stage line reporting a check already performed; it only reports a check rather than delivering one.

entities.span: Test it: `/test eval harness runner` · 27 tests across three files, closing **one of the two gaps** `verify.md` recorded.
rejected_spans: `test/helpers/eval-report.test.ts` (21) covers the printed table and the JSON file: the header, the filter line both ways, every row carrying its denominator, the per cause failure lines, `skipped` against `incomplete`, the abort line, all four preference leak outcomes, and the filename's colon replacement. `test/helpers/eval-filter.test.ts` (4) covers the `-t` channel AC-8 rests on. `tiers.test.ts` gained 2 for `resolvedModel()`, whose refusal branch was never exercised. Each of the seven guarded behaviours was broken on purpose after the commit hooks ran and each failed. The report test deliberately lives in `test/helpers/`, not beside `report.ts`, because `test/eval/**` is the paid project and widening the free suite's `include` to reach it would pull the 80 call harness into `pnpm test`.
entities.unclassified_note: A stage line reporting tests already written and run; it only reports a check rather than delivering a build step.

entities.span: **Corrected 2026-09-08 after review**: this line first claimed both recorded gaps were closed. Only the `report.ts` one was. The second, `harness.test.ts`'s own inline orchestration, stayed untested, and the Fable review found a real defect living in exactly it: Vitest runs `afterAll` even when `beforeAll` threw, so a run that never started wrote a report reading `status: "completed"` with all sixteen pairs `skipped`, a refused run described as a full run that scored nothing. That orchestration is now **partly** covered: the report assembly moved out of the `afterAll` into `buildEvalReport()` in `test/eval/report.ts`, with nine more free tests over it including the not started branch, taking `eval-report.test.ts` to 30 and these three files to 36. What is still inline in the `afterAll`, the hook ordering and the fixture user cleanup, remains provable only by a paid run
entities.unclassified_note: A correction note on the test stage line's earlier claim; it reports test coverage status and fits no named type.

entities.span: This tier carries no `Review it` or `Document it` box, so the round that ran is recorded here instead, the same way feature 15's is. Reviewed 2026-09-08 on **Fable 5.1** against an Opus 5 author, 17 files, verdict **Changes requested**: one major, five minors, seven nits.
entities.unclassified_note: A record of a review round that took place; it states no requirement, outcome or build step.

entities.span: **The remaining five minors and seven nits are open**, recorded in the findings file; the one worth acting on first is that the three preference pair ids in `eval-verdict.ts` are untied to `PAIRS`, so a rename would silently disable AC-5 and still exit 0.

Across two full sixteen pair runs on 2026-09-08, read per pair from each report's `distribution` field: `control-one-gap` returned `good_match` 1 and `possible_match` 4 in the 07:30 run and `possible_match` 5 in the 07:35 run, against an expected `good_match`, so it failed both; `key-domain-mismatch` returned `weak_match` 3 and `not_a_match` 2, then `not_a_match` 5, against an expected `not_a_match`, so it failed the first and passed the second.
entities.unclassified_note: A recorded finding from harness runs; it states no requirement and fits no named type.

entities.span: `control-one-gap` is corrected to `possible_match` and no anchor changes.
entities.unclassified_note: A recorded outcome of spec 0018's review of data; it fits no named type.

entities.span: The `weak_match` and `not_a_match` boundary that spec 0016's `boundary-seniority-gap` rationale names as a gap in `BAND_ANCHORS` is still undefined, and stays recorded as a gap there rather than being closed on one split pair.
